edits.old: AWS VPC Traffic Mirroring is not universally zero-impact: AWS documentation says mirrored packets count toward source-instance bandwidth and may be dropped when bandwidth or packet-rate limits are exceeded. The AWS blog's no-performance-impact statement is specific to its out-of-band architecture and should not be generalized to every mirroring setup. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
edits.new: AWS VPC Traffic Mirroring is not zero-impact in every case: mirrored traffic counts toward the source instance's bandwidth, and mirrored traffic is dropped when the instance's bandwidth or packet-per-second limits are exceeded (production traffic is prioritized, but is also dropped if it alone keeps exceeding the limits). The AWS blog's statement that VPC Traffic Mirroring replicates traffic out-of-band with no performance impact describes that blog's out-of-band design, and the limitations page shows the instance-level caveats. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-network-limitations.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/mirror-production-traffic-to-test-environment-with-vpc-traffic-mirroring/

edits.old: Shadow traffic is not automatically side-effect-free. A state-changing request may execute on both versions, and shared state such as a cache can alter or contaminate performance measurements. Isolate candidate data and downstream effects, or make replayed operations safe to repeat. (high confidence)
edits.new: Shadow traffic is not automatically side-effect-free. Mirrored requests can be processed twice, so an idempotent application is needed when requests must only be processed once, and shared state such as a cache between canary and production can inflate the cache hit rate and invalidate performance measurements. Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/mirror-production-traffic-to-test-environment-with-vpc-traffic-mirroring/ ; https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/

evidence.quote: Compared to traffic splitting, traffic mirroring has the additional requirement of preventing data duplication.
an idempotent application is needed when requests must only be processed once even if duplicate requests are received
if the canary deployment and production systems share a cache, an artificially inflated cache hit rate would invalidate performance measurements for the canary metrics.

edits.old: Shadowing leaves the stable version on the client response path and sends a copy of each selected request to the candidate; the candidate response is discarded and does not delay the primary response. This exercises the candidate on real request inputs without exposing its output to users. (high confidence)
edits.new: With traffic mirroring, all requests are routed to the base version and replayed to the new version; the client receives responses only from the base version and the new version's responses are discarded. In Envoy's implementation, shadowing is fire and forget: Envoy does not wait for the shadow cluster to respond before returning the primary cluster's response. Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/mirror-production-traffic-to-test-environment-with-vpc-traffic-mirroring/ ; https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto
